_comment: Routing here is deliberately narrow. `web-quality-skills:accessibility` is the REMEDIATION skill for the same standard — 'audit and improve', with the corrected markup beside every rule — so the two descriptions share most of their vocabulary and only the verb separates them. The negatives below are the remediation asks: a user who says 'make my site accessible' or 'fix the contrast' wants the maker, not this findings-only auditor.

positive.prompt: Run an accessibility audit of my checkout flow and write up what fails
Audit this app against WCAG 2.2 and give me a prioritized report
I need an a11y report on the signup screen before we ship

negative.prompt: Fix the color contrast on my buttons and add the missing ARIA labels
Optimize Core Web Vitals and reduce my layout shift

evals.prompt: Clone and run https://github.com/carlsz/sprout, then run a live accessibility audit of its add / edit / complete / delete task flows.
evals.expected_output: A contract-valid accessibility report under Sprout/.ux/audits/ whose findings each cite a WCAG 2.2 criterion with its level, carry a P0-P3 priority justified by impact on the affected user, and are backed by measurements or accessibility-tree evidence; one health item per criterion actually checked.
expectations: Writes a report to Sprout/.ux/audits/accessibility-<timestamp>.md that validates against the shared report contract, with auditor: accessibility
Every finding cites its criterion by number, name and level (e.g. 'WCAG 2.2 — 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum), Level AA')
No finding's priority is taken from its conformance level: each Priority field names the affected user and the tie-breaker that decided it
The health scorecard carries one item per criterion actually checked and no others — criteria that were not evaluated appear in the appendix coverage list instead
Runtime-bound findings (contrast, focus order, focus visibility, target size) are stated as verified in live mode, backed by a measurement, screenshot or accessibility-tree excerpt
If automated tooling was run, the appendix says what it covered and no '0 violations' result is reported as 'accessible'
Does not edit any of Sprout's application code, however small the fix looks
All writes are confined to Sprout/.ux/audits/

evals.prompt: Run a static accessibility audit of https://github.com/carlsz/sprout from source only, without starting the app.
evals.expected_output: A contract-valid static report that settles the markup-bound criteria and labels every runtime-bound finding 'potential — unverified', stating in the appendix that a static run cannot establish conformance.
expectations: Reports mode: static in the frontmatter and the appendix
Markup-bound criteria (1.1.1, 1.3.1, 3.1.1, 3.3.2, 4.1.2) are settled from source with file:line evidence
Every runtime-bound finding — contrast, focus order, focus visibility, target size, live regions — is labeled 'potential — unverified' with the reason
The appendix states that a static run cannot establish conformance
No contrast ratio is asserted as a measurement without a computed render
